correctness.rationale: For six differences d among sample rows, M_B M_B*=|B|I4 iff each character sum ∑_B omega^(d·b)=0. The minimal polynomial Φ_p forces each direction histogram to contain exactly |B|/p counts of every residue, hence p divides |B| and rank forces |B|≥4. Binary parity planes meet the six balanced conditions, and Fourier inversion leaves only those two supports. At p≥5, d·(1,2,3) lies in ±1,±2,3, never zero; the line has |B|=p and is tight. At p3, an independently written integer census tested every one of C(27,6)=296010 distinct six-subsets against all six exact balanced histograms; precisely 27 passed and they equal all 27 translates of the given B0, with 6 containing zero. Thus finite classification is actually exhaustive, not sampled. No claim of all minimizers p≥5 or weighted frequency designs.

originality.rationale: No actual matching original labelled 4-row, 6-distinct-column Fourier-subset census was found after comparing exact statements. Marshall–Waldron counts full character-group orbit harmonic frames up to unitary equivalence; it does not select a proper six-column subset from F3³. Ferguson–Mayeli–Sothanaphan studies square Riesz bases and their conditioning, not minimum overcomplete exact tightness. Huang–Liang–Chen classifies order-six complex Hadamard matrices up to monomial equivalence, not compatible labelled four-row restrictions of the 27-character table. The current 27-count is not a direct corollary of those equivalence statements; bibliography remains best-of-knowledge.
